title: Tenanted Proxy Readiness Index and Fasttrack Concierge Playbook
creator: Aisha Bennett
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers requesting Private/VPC/on-prem installs often surface non-uniform networking constraints (proxy auth, strict egress, deep inspection, strict TLS interceptors) that block onboarding. Current intake is manual and inconsistent: some requests are fast-tracked with engineering concierge time while others stall due to incomplete signals.

Goal: Define a scoring index (Tenanted Proxy Readiness Index, TPRI) to automatically classify network readiness for onboarding, plus a documented concierge fasttrack lane and remediation playbook so PMs and Solutions Engineers can triage and commit consistent SLAs for triage and rollouts. This ticket codifies the index, acceptance criteria, triage SOP, and handoff to ENG for automation hooks (probes and intake API).

Why now: Increasing private deployment requests have stretched concierge bandwidth, causing long lead times and customer frustration; automating the initial triage and surfacing clear remediation steps reduces average time-to-first-success and improves CSAT for high-commitment customers.
acceptance_criteria: TPRI definition and scoring rubric published to Confluence with examples for 6 common proxy patterns (transparent, auth header, NTLM/Negotiate, MTLS-offload, TLS intercept, egress-only)
Intake form updated in self-serve portal to capture the 12 signals used by TPRI (eg. proxy_type, allowed_domains, egress_ports, outbound_ips, requires_client_cert, bastion_present)
Concierge fasttrack lane documented with SLA: initial contact within 48 hours for TPRI >= 70, escalation path for >90 customers, and standard remediation recipes for TPRI buckets (<30, 30-69, >=70)
Automation hooks defined for ENG: a lightweight probe pattern (safe TCP/SNI/HTTP HEAD probes) and API contract for intake response (TPRI score + suggested remediation entries)
Pilot with 3 incoming enterprise customers executed and time-to-onboard measured; target 30% reduction vs baseline onboarding time
Confluence playbook includes clear security checklist and KMS/HSM notes for air-gapped and VPC customers
tasks: Draft TPRI scoring rubric and threshold buckets
Update intake form fields and validation rules in product portal (UX spec)
Create Confluence playbook with remediation recipes and escalation matrix
Work with ENG to define probe API and safety constraints
Create training doc and Slack snippets for Solutions Engineering concierge
Run pilot onboarding for three customers and record telemetry
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): finalize rubric, update intake form, and publish Confluence playbook. Phase 2 (3 weeks): ENG implement probe API and automation stub; Solutions Eng training; start pilot with 3 customers. Phase 3 (2 weeks): iterate on thresholds based on pilot, enable automated TPRI calculation in intake flow, and instrument metrics (time_to_first_success, escalations, CSAT). Roll to general intake after internal signoff and security review.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: aggressive probe heuristics reduce manual follow-up but risk false negatives in strict air-gapped environments — probes must be opt-in and respect customer-requested no-probe flag.
Tradeoff: a higher TPRI threshold reduces false positives for fasttrack but may increase manual labor — pilot will inform optimal cutpoints.
Decision: start with read-only passive probes (DNS/TCP SNI/HTTP HEAD) and require customer permission for any active TLS or client-cert checks.
Risk: customers with regulatory constraints may not be able to provide signals; include a fallback human-review lane and standard questionnaire.
